PyTorch hooks run through `module(...)`; calling `module.forward(...)` directly bypasses them, and custom methods such as `log2feats` do not automatically trigger the root module’s hooks. Recommended verification: invoke the actual NextItNet prediction entry point, attach a counter and sentinel exception to a child module it must execute, and assert that the exception reaches the caller. Register temporary hooks inside `try/finally` and always call `handle.remove()`. `always_call=True` enables hook execution after forward failures; it does not remove hooks. [Module documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Module.html)

For exception-safe isolation, snapshot every module’s individual `training` flag, cloned parameters, all buffers—including nonpersistent buffers—and existing gradients. Restore flags individually because recursive `train(flag)` can overwrite mixed training/evaluation modes. A plain `state_dict()` snapshot is insufficient: its tensors reference live model storage and it excludes nonpersistent buffers. Use evaluation mode plus disabled gradients for inference probes. Preserve Python/NumPy RNGs and explicit generators separately; `torch.random.fork_rng(devices=[device])` restores CPU and selected CUDA RNG states. [Module state](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Module.html), [RNG context](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.15/random.html)

DataLoader iteration can consume RNG and advance samplers, workers and prefetch queues; restoring global RNG alone cannot establish unchanged data execution. Prefer cached diagnostic batches or an isolated loader with independent generators and sampler state. Recommended regression: compare untouched execution against successful-probe and injected-failure execution from identical starting states; assert restored hooks, flags, tensors, gradients, RNGs, next training batch, prediction scores and next optimization step. This tests preservation while retaining one trained model. [DataLoader randomness](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/docs/source/data.md)
